newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico's sharp GDP rise well-received.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico's sharp GDP rise well-received.

text.p: Mexico's strong second quarter gross domestic product growth -- 8.8 percent compared to the second quarter of 1996 -- was welcomed by analysts as good news for the Mexican economy.
"Obviously it was extremely strong," IDEA economist Gene Frieda told Reuters.
"But you have to take it with a grain of salt, since part of it was payback from the first quarter as we had more working days in the second quarter (because of Easter)," he said.
Discounting the Easter effect, second quarter GDP rose 7.4 percent, the Finance Ministry said
"But it is very positive for what it says about the state of private consumption and the service sector," Frieda said.
The Finance Ministry said first half GDP rose 7.0 percent against the same period a year earlier.
A survey of 13 Mexico City offices of brokerages and reasearch forms found expectations of a second quarter GDP rise of 5.92 percent.
The survey was taken before higher-than-expected industrial production figures were released on Thursday.
Interacciones economist Alonso Cervera said the GDP number "was an excellent surprise."
"The implication is very clear, and that is that private consumption is stronger than many people thought," he said.

Economists said the strong number will likely cause an increase in forecasts for growth for the year. Cervera said a GDP number for the year of more than 6.0 percent would be "the most likely scenerio."
MMS International said higher-than-expected trade surpluses and industrial production contributed to a surprising economic expansion.
"Markets may look for a higher end-of-year GDP forecast," MMS said in a market report.
